title: Teaching Agents to Search with NVIDIA Data Designer — Dhruv Nathawani, NVIDIA
talk_summary: NVIDIA's Dhruv Nathawani demos NeMo Data Designer, an open-source framework that builds synthetic-data pipelines as a DAG of columns (seed data, Python samplers, LLM/structured columns, LLM-as-judge) to generate training data, using agentic search (Tavily via MCP) as the worked example. The transferable parts are the data-generation discipline: diversity-before-volume, cheapest-correct-column-type, overproduce-then-filter, preview-before-batch, and layered evaluation of synthetic data.

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate far more candidate records than needed, then funnel through LLM-as-judge plus deterministic checks plus human spot-checks, keeping only high-quality records.
Take LLM-as-judge outputs and have human reviewers cross-check the judgments to establish confidence in the judge.
Use deterministic Python for anything that doesn't need an LLM (samplers, structure) and reserve LLM calls for genuinely generative steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you always want to use the cheapest correct column type ... using a LLM to create a sampler makes no sense

takeaways.what_they_do: Run a 3-record preview, inspect outputs, adjust prompts/workflow, and only then launch the full batch; treat generation as iterative, not one-and-done.
takeaways.evidence_quote: data creation is very iterative. It's not like one and done ... iterate on it and then once you're happy with it, you can send it off to batch execution

takeaways.what_they_do: Inject varied seed values into prompt templates at runtime so every prompt is unique, and weight samplers to control distribution.

takeaways.technique: Constrained tool-use instructions with in-context example
takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent one tool plus explicit usage guidelines (don't over-call, cost limits) and a worked example trajectory in the prompt.
